subject: Post-call: OpenFin discovery — cost pressure, quantization appetite, proposed pilot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Holt <jared.holt@openfin.io>
Cc: OpenFin FinOps <finops@openfin.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: OpenFin discovery — cost pressure, quantization appetite, proposed pilot

Hi Jared / FinOps team,

Thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier — good conversation and helped surface the key constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points we heard
- Unit economics: ~ $120k/mo token spend today (mostly embeddings + long-context generation). Margin sensitivity on per-token cost.
- Latency spikes at p95 during batch jobs and live session bursts — impacts product SLAs.
- Limited caching today: in-house prefix cache but no KV reuse across models.
- Risk tolerance: willing to trade some throughput for 15–20% cost reduction; quality loss must be small for critical flows.

What you told us about stack
- Serving: self-hosted Triton + some TF-serving endpoints on GCP; a small portion on managed endpoints.
- Orchestration: internal request broker (k8s) and an S3-based trace archive (you shared link).
- Current optimizations: batching for async jobs, limited prefix caching for chat threads.

Success criteria (as discussed)
- Achieve >=15% reduction in per-token unit cost for main gen workloads without >2–3% regression in prompt-level quality metrics.
- p95 latency at or under 220ms for interactive flows during normal load (burst handling as a stretch).
- Clear audit trail + telemetry to validate cost/quality changes.

What we propose (next steps)
1) Technical deep-dive: schedule 60m with our Solutions Engineer (bring model/infra folks) to review traces and latency profiles.
2) Pilot: 4-week cost pilot aiming to prove batching, prefix cache, and an int8 quantization profile on a shadow subset. Deliverables: cost delta analysis, latency report, and quality evals on your golden prompt set.
3) Share artifacts: I attached a short scenarios workbook (redwood-cost-scenarios.xlsx) and a pilot-outline.pdf to make the pilot concrete.

Requests from your side
- Share representative traces (S3 link you mentioned) and a small set of golden prompts for quality checking.
- Confirm internal stakeholders for the tech deep-dive (model owners, infra).

If this looks right, I can: (a) lock in the deep-dive timeslots next week, (b) loop in Marissa to draft the pilot SOW, and (c) have Neha prep an optimization/config checklist.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0149

Attachments: redwood-cost-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs), pilot-outline.pdf (1 page)
From: Jared Holt <jared.holt@openfin.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: OpenFin FinOps <finops@openfin.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: OpenFin discovery — cost pressure, quantization appetite, proposed pilot

Vivek — thanks, this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications and answers inline.

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 2:05 PM -0800 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Pain points we heard
> - Unit economics: ~ $120k/mo token spend today (mostly embeddings + long-context generation). Margin sensitivity on per-token cost.

Correct — that $120k is our estimated billable token spend; embeddings are ~45% of that.

> - Latency spikes at p95 during batch jobs and live session bursts — impacts product SLAs.

Yes. Live sessions are the real pain point. We need predictable p95 under load.

> Willingness to trade throughput for 15–20% cost reduction; quality loss must be small.

Agreed. We are open to int8-ish quantization but we need pre/post-eval on our golden set first. If quality dips more than ~2% on our metrics, we need rollback.

> Requests: Share traces and golden prompts

Link to the traces (read-only): s3://openfin-prod/traces/2026-11-18/trace-agg.json
Golden prompts: I uploaded a 150-row CSV to the same bucket (golden_prompts.csv).

Timeline: We can be ready to start a pilot in ~2 weeks. Please send a pilot SOW and an estimated cost delta for both hosted and Dedicated flows. Also include an estimate for the instrumentation work (tracing + eval harness).

Thanks — Jared
Jared Holt
Head of FinOps, OpenFin
jared.holt@openfin.io
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: OpenFin discovery — cost pressure, quantization appetite, proposed pilot

Folks — forwarding the thread from OpenFin. Key asks: pilot in ~2 weeks, int8 openness with <2% quality regression tolerance, traces/golden prompts uploaded to S3, target >=15% unit-cost reduction.

My suggested approach:
- Marissa: draft a 4-week pilot SOW (scope: shadow eval + small dedicated pool / hosted split, instrumentation + quality eval).
- Neha: prepare an optimization checklist and a baseline run plan (what configs to try first: batching windows, prefix cache config, KV hit measurement, int8 profile).
- I'll set up the technical deep-dive and bring a solutions engineer.

Risks to call out to the customer: time to integrate traces (~2–3 days), possible model-accuracy variability with quantization — need an automated rollback plan.

Marissa / Neha, any modifications before I send the SOW and propose timeslots?

— Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: OpenFin discovery — cost pressure, quantization appetite, proposed pilot

Looks good. Quick notes:
- I'll draft the SOW today and include two options: (A) hosted-first quick pilot (lower friction), (B) dedicated pool pilot (higher fidelity for cost proofs).
- Neha: will need an initial config matrix from you by EOD tomorrow so I can slot the evaluation steps.
- Vivek: I'll also include an estimated budget range (based on the redwood-cost-scenarios.xlsx) and a short approval checklist for procurement.

I can have a SOW draft and proposed deep-dive slots by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa
